article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: Amnesia × OG #18
Breeder: BC Bud Depot
THC Content: 25-28%
CBD Content: 1%
Terpene Profile: Limonene , myrcene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Earth, citrus, pine, sour fuel, herbs
Flowering Time (Indoor): 63–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late October
Indoor Yield: 500–600 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate to advanced

Honey OG is not named for an overwhelmingly sugary flavor. Its character is more rugged than that name suggests, combining damp earth, bright citrus rind, pine resin, sour fuel, and occasional floral sweetness into an aroma that feels firmly rooted in classic OG cannabis. BC Bud Depot created the strain by crossing an award-winning European Amnesia selection with OG #18, bringing together cerebral Haze-influenced energy and one of the more celebrated sour phenotypes of OG Kush . The result is a balanced hybrid whose personality shifts noticeably as the experience develops rather than remaining fixed in either an uplifting or sedating direction.

That balance extends to the plant itself. Honey OG can stretch enough to require planning indoors, yet it produces dense, heavily resinous flowers that reveal the Kush side of the pedigree. Potency may reach the upper 20% THC range in strong selections, making this cannabis strain considerably more powerful than its earthy-citrus flavor initially implies. Growers should also understand that this is not a cultivar that rewards neglect. It can react poorly to excessive fertilizer or water, but attentive cultivation can produce aromatic weed with thick trichomes and the kind of sour OG depth that remains appealing long after sweeter modern hybrids have blurred together.
Genetics and Lineage

The breeder-documented parentage is Amnesia crossed with OG #18. The Amnesia side supplies the more cerebral half of the equation. European Amnesia genetics became famous for combining Haze -like mental intensity with more manageable commercial characteristics, producing marijuana associated with citrus, incense, herbs, spice, and an energetic high. Different Amnesia lines have circulated for decades, so assigning an exact deeper genealogy to the specific BC Bud Depot parent would go beyond what the breeder formally documented. What matters here is that the selected parent came from award-winning European stock chosen for potency and quality.

OG #18 is much better defined. Also known as Private Reserve OG, it originated as a prized phenotype selected from OG Kush genetics by Reserva Privada . The #18 selection became valued for a sourer, more fuel-driven aroma than standard OG Kush, improved yield, hard resinous flowers, and substantial potency. Its sensory profile leans toward gasoline, damp earth, pine, lemon, and sour Kush, which explains why those qualities remain so obvious in Honey OG despite the brighter Amnesia influence.

Crossing the two creates a hybrid that sits close to an even indica-sativa balance. Amnesia contributes vertical vigor, mental energy, and brighter aromatic qualities, while OG #18 adds dense buds, sour fuel, resin production, and greater physical depth. Instead of either parent disappearing, the finished cultivar often feels like a conversation between them: Haze-influenced cerebral activity on top and OG relaxation developing underneath.
Effects and Experience

Honey OG can begin with a strong mental presence. The first portion of the high may feel clear, animated, and increasingly euphoric, making music, conversation, creative work, or an unstructured walk more engaging. There is often a progressive quality rather than a sudden wall of intoxication; mental intensity builds for several minutes, giving experienced consumers time to notice the shift before the full strength becomes apparent. At moderate doses, that phase can feel sociable and mentally expansive without immediately compromising physical comfort.

Later, the OG #18 side begins to change the tone. The body relaxes, muscular tension becomes less distracting, and the energetic edge of the Amnesia influence starts to soften. Interestingly, the cerebral component does not always disappear; some consumers may feel waves of renewed mental activity even while the body remains calm. At high doses, however, THC approaching the upper 20% range can become overwhelming. Dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, racing thoughts, or temporary anxiety are possible when too much is consumed, particularly for people sensitive to stimulating cannabis. Careful dosing preserves the strain’s unusual combination of mental lift and grounded physical relaxation far better than heavy consumption.
Medical Benefits

Medical cannabis consumers may find the cultivar interesting because it does not commit entirely to either daytime stimulation or nighttime sedation. The mentally uplifting opening may be useful to some people dealing with fatigue, stress, or low motivation, while the later physical calm may help make muscular tension or persistent discomfort less intrusive. THC interacts with the endocannabinoid system and additional neurological pathways involved in pain perception, mood, appetite, and sensory processing, but individual responses can vary substantially even when two people consume the same flower.

Because CBD levels are generally low, Honey OG should be considered a THC-dominant medicinal option rather than a balanced cannabinoid strain. People prone to anxiety may find the Amnesia side too mentally active at larger doses, while those seeking immediate sleep may prefer a heavier indica. Limonene, myrcene, caryophyllene, and pinene can appear prominently in similar expressions of the cultivar, contributing citrus, earth, pepper, and pine. These aromatic compounds add complexity to the experience but should not be treated as guaranteed treatments for any particular condition.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Earth and citrus form the most dependable aromatic foundation. The first smell from cured flower can resemble rain-darkened soil mixed with lemon rind, followed by pine and a more acidic, sour quality as the bud is broken apart. OG #18 adds fuel and Kush pungency, while the Amnesia side may contribute lighter floral, herbal, or incense-like notes. Certain plants can show a faint honeyed sweetness, but it usually sits in the background rather than dominating the profile.

On the palate, the flavor often starts earthy before sharp citrus and pine become more obvious through the middle of the inhale. Sour fuel may linger on the exhale, accompanied by pepper, herbs, and mild floral sweetness. Limonene supports the citrus brightness, while myrcene can deepen the earthy component and beta-caryophyllene contributes spice. Vaporization tends to expose more of the lemon, pine, and floral qualities, whereas combustion pushes the heavier Kush, fuel, and earth characteristics forward. Slow drying and a controlled cure are especially important because the brighter top notes disappear quickly from overdried cannabis.
Growing Information

Honey OG is better suited to growers willing to pay attention than to those looking for a completely forgiving plant. BC Bud Depot has described the strain as somewhat temperamental, particularly when exposed to excessive watering or aggressive feeding. The Amnesia influence can produce meaningful stretch during the transition into bloom, so indoor growers should avoid allowing vegetative plants to fill all available vertical space before flowering begins. Topping, low-stress training, and an evenly developed canopy can help control height while increasing the number of productive flower sites.

Indoor flowering generally takes approximately 63–70 days, placing the strain in the nine-to-ten-week range. Under optimized conditions, production can fall around 500–600 grams per square meter, though actual yield depends heavily on phenotype, light intensity, plant density, root health, training, and environmental control. Flowers become increasingly dense and resinous during the later weeks, and branches may require support once the buds gain weight. Rather than pushing nutrient concentration upward in pursuit of larger yields, growers usually benefit from reading the plant carefully and avoiding salt accumulation or chronically saturated root zones.

Outdoor cultivation works best where autumn remains warm and relatively dry into late October. The relatively late finish makes Honey OG less suitable for northern gardens that experience heavy rain or early frost during October. Given strong sunlight, generous root volume, and a long vegetative period, plants can become substantially larger than indoor specimens and produce respectable harvests. Airflow is especially important as dense OG-influenced flowers mature. Resin production also gives the crop useful potential for dry sift, water hash, and rosin, particularly when harvest timing is chosen with trichome maturity and terpene preservation in mind rather than maximum flower weight alone.
FAQ
What strains make Honey OG?

BC Bud Depot created Honey OG by crossing an award-winning European Amnesia selection with OG #18. Amnesia contributes the brighter cerebral character and Haze-influenced aroma, while OG #18 adds sour fuel, pine, dense flowers, heavy resin, and greater physical relaxation.
Is Honey OG indica or sativa?

The original BC Bud Depot version is approximately 50% indica and 50% sativa. Its effects reflect that balance unusually well. Mental stimulation and euphoria tend to appear first, while physical relaxation builds later without necessarily eliminating the cerebral component.
How strong is Honey OG?

High-potency selections have been reported at roughly 28% THC or more, although actual laboratory results depend on phenotype, cultivation environment, harvest maturity, curing, and testing methodology. CBD is generally very low. Because the Amnesia influence can make the high mentally intense, even experienced cannabis consumers may prefer moderate doses.
What does Honey OG taste like?

Earth, citrus, pine, sour fuel, herbs, and mild floral sweetness form the central flavor profile. The OG #18 parent contributes much of the pungent Kush and gasoline character, while Amnesia supplies brighter citrus, herbal, and occasionally incense-like qualities. The “Honey” name should not be interpreted as meaning the strain tastes primarily of sugary honey.
How long does Honey OG take to flower?

Indoor flowering normally takes approximately 63–70 days, or about nine to ten weeks. Outdoors, plants generally require a long enough season to finish around late October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates. Trichome maturity, flower swelling, plant health, and local weather should determine the exact harvest date.
Final Thoughts on Honey OG

Honey OG succeeds because its parents bring opposite strengths without producing a confused hybrid. Amnesia contributes cerebral energy, brightness, and European Haze influence; OG #18 answers with sour fuel, hard resinous flowers, pine, earth, and the unmistakable physical weight of a selected OG Kush phenotype. The final plant preserves both sides instead of reducing them to a generic middle ground.

That genetic balance makes the strain appealing but also slightly demanding. Growers receive substantial resin and strong yield potential, yet the plant prefers attentive irrigation and nutrition and needs enough time to finish a nine-to-ten-week bloom cycle. Consumers encounter a similarly layered experience: mental energy arrives first, body relaxation follows, and strong doses can reveal just how potent the combination can become.

For people seeking sweet candy weed, Honey OG may not fit expectations. Its appeal is more traditional and considerably more rugged—citrus rind over damp earth, pine beside sour fuel, and just enough floral sweetness to keep the profile from becoming harsh. In a market increasingly crowded with dessert-oriented hybrids, that earthy OG character gives the cultivar a distinctive identity.

Honey OG ultimately works best for growers and consumers who appreciate balance without blandness. It offers the bright cerebral side of Amnesia, the heavy resin and fuel of OG #18, high THC potential, and a flavor rooted in classic Kush rather than novelty. When cultivated carefully and allowed to mature fully, it remains a compelling example of what happens when strong European Haze genetics meet one of the more celebrated OG Kush selections.
